truthAudit.Summary: Audit of Run 2 against the 20 true vulnerabilities of enhanced_calc.cpp. Run 2 correctly detected 11 vulnerabilities as found_full (SC-V3-001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 009, 010, 011, 020), 1 as found_partial (SC-V3-013, found the vulnerable code region but misclassified CWE-78 instead of CWE-377), and missed 8 (SC-V3-008, 012, 014, 015, 016, 017, 018, 019). No overclaims were made. The main discrepancies are severity under-reporting (Critical/High downgraded to High/Medium/Low) and two CWE misclassifications (CWE-120 vs CWE-122, CWE-489 vs CWE-511, CWE-78 vs CWE-377). Run 2 also reported several findings not in the true list (execute_admin_command system, append_override_audit_event system, safe_string_copy off-by-one, format_string template) which are real latent patterns.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: printf uses active_format as the format string (line 238). runtime_log_format() defaults to config::security::LOG_FORMAT
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #1 (log_debug_message, CWE-134) directly identifies the printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) format-string path via runtime_log_format(), matching the true anchor set.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: for (long long i = 2; i <= static_cast<long long>(x); i++) { result *= i; }
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #14 (fact function, CWE-190) identifies the result *= i cumulative multiplication overflow, matching the true anchor result *= i / fact.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Worker threads that later read scratch access freed memory, causing memory corruption / potential RCE.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #6 (stage_deferred_history_flush vs g_memory_pool.cleanup, CWE-416) identifies the use-after-free with scratch pointer captured by enqueued task and pool freed without join, matching the true anchors.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: An attacker controlling the config file can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. validator_path='x; rm -rf /') to achieve command execution.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #7 (validate_config, CWE-78) identifies validator_cmd + " " + config_file passed to system(), matching the true anchors.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: When the input length is >= buffer size, the code deliberately uses unbounded strcpy, overflowing the stack buffer.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #3 (evaluate_expression, CWE-120) identifies the strcpy(input_buffer_, ...) unbounded copy on the stack member, matching the true anchors.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: value_ is read outside the lock into old_value, then written inside the lock. Concurrent increments can read the same stale value and overwrite each other, causing lost updates and a data race.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #11 (ThreadSafeCounter::increment, CWE-362) identifies the read-modify-write outside the lock on volatile long long value_, matching the true anchors.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: After more than five failed logins, merely containing the substring 'EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE' in the input grants full authentication, bypassing the real password check.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #5 (authenticate, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE) identifies the login_attempts_ > 5 / EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE / authenticated_ = true backdoor, matching the true anchors.

Run 2 never flags config_dir_ + filename (line 543) concatenation passed to load_config as path traversal; the load_config mentions are only in the command-injection context. The CWE-22 path traversal was not detected.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: expression_buffer_ is a 256-byte pool allocation but strcpy (line 376) copies the entire concatenated token string with no length check.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #2 (ExpressionParser::parse, CWE-120) identifies the unbounded strcpy into the 256-byte expression_buffer_ allocated via schedule_expression_analysis, matching the true anchors.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: The admin credential is embedded in the source (and thus in the binary). Anyone with source/binary access can authenticate as admin.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #9 (ADMIN_SECRET, CWE-798) identifies the hardcoded 'SC_ENT_2025_AUTH' credential, matching the true anchors.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Session tokens are drawn from only 9000 possible values (1000-9999), making them trivially brute-forceable and allowing session hijacking of admin sessions.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #8 (generate_session_token, CWE-338) identifies the mt19937 + uniform_int_distribution(1000, 9999) weak PRNG, matching the true anchors.

Run 2's log_debug_message finding focuses on the printf format string; it never flags the static std::tm cached_time assigned from localtime() (lines 230-231) as a thread-unsafe timestamp race. Not detected.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: The shell command embeds the TMPDIR-derived path into a 'sh -c' invocation.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #13 identified the exact append_override_audit_event code (TMPDIR, supercalc_emergency.log, system) but classified it as command injection (CWE-78) rather than the true insecure temporary file handling (CWE-377). Partial detection of the vulnerable region with a misclassified vulnerability type.

Run 2 never flags persistent authentication state (authenticated_, login_attempts_, session_token_ surviving across sessions, CWE-613). login_attempts_ is a static atomic that persists; this was not detected.
Run 2 never flags std::stod(tokens[3]) in handle_variable_command (line 729) throwing an unhandled std::invalid_argument before the catch. Not detected.
Run 2 never flags the integer underflow in MemoryPool::allocate block split (previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES, line 133). Not detected.
Run 2 never flags the unbounded recursion (parse_expression -> parse_term -> parse_factor -> parse_expression on PAREN_OPEN, lines 426-430). Not detected.
Run 2 never flags the data race in ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached (result_cache_ accessed without cache_mutex_ across thread_pool_->enqueue tasks). Not detected.
Run 2 never flags the TOCTOU in load_config (std::filesystem::exists then sleep_for then std::ifstream, lines 544-546). Not detected.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: For empty input or input beginning with whitespace, token_length is 0, so '100 / 0' is integer division by zero (UB, typically SIGFPE), crashing the process.
Items.Notes: Run 2 finding #10 (calculate_route_score, CWE-369) identifies the 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) division-by-zero, matching the true anchors.
